summary: Saudi Arabia offers citizens of around 60 countries a one-year multiple-entry tourist eVisa (with mandatory medical insurance bundled into the fee) allowing stays of up to 90 days, gives the same group and holders of valid US, UK or Schengen visas a visa on arrival, and routes everyone else through embassy visas or the separate Hajj and Umrah regimes.

Visit Saudi — eVisa requirements

vaccinations.name: Meningococcal ACWY
vaccinations.certificate: Vaccination certificate (quadrivalent ACWY, issued within the validity period and at least 10 days before arrival)
vaccinations.text: Pilgrims traveling for Hajj or Umrah must show a valid quadrivalent meningococcal ACWY vaccination certificate. It is not required for ordinary tourist entry, but tourists planning to perform Umrah should carry one. Additional seasonal requirements (e.g. polio or yellow fever for arrivals from specific countries) apply during Hajj — check the Ministry of Health requirements for your departure country.

source.name: Saudi Ministry of Health — Hajj and Umrah health requirements

travelInsurance.text: Medical insurance is mandatory for tourist eVisa and visa-on-arrival visitors — a policy from a Saudi-approved insurer is bundled automatically into the visa fee, so no separate purchase is needed.

source.name: Visit Saudi — eVisa insurance information

onwardTicket.text: Onward tickets are not systematically checked for tourist eVisa holders, but airlines and border officers may ask for proof of return travel and accommodation.

source.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Saudi Arabia

proofOfFunds.text: No fixed amount is published; border officers may ask visitors to show sufficient means for their stay.

source.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Saudi Arabia

currencyLimits.text: Cash and negotiable instruments worth SAR 60,000 or more (or the foreign-currency equivalent) must be declared on arrival and departure.

source.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Saudi Arabia

notes: Alcohol, pork products, narcotics and pornographic material are strictly prohibited — there is no duty-free alcohol allowance and importing any amount is an offense.
Many medications (codeine, tramadol, sedatives, CBD) are controlled — carry the original prescription and check the rules before traveling.
Drug offenses carry extremely severe penalties, including the death penalty for trafficking.

payments.text: Cards and contactless payments (mada, Visa, Mastercard, Apple Pay) are accepted almost everywhere, including taxis and small shops. Cash is only occasionally useful in traditional souqs and rural areas.

safety.text: Saudi Arabia has low street crime and is generally safe for tourists. The main risks are legal and cultural (strict laws on drugs, alcohol and public behavior) plus occasional regional missile or drone threats near the Yemen border — avoid the border area and monitor the news.

source.name: U.S. Department of State — Saudi Arabia Travel Advisory

bestTimeToVisit.text: November to February brings mild, sunny weather ideal for Riyadh, AlUla and the Red Sea coast; summer temperatures regularly exceed 45°C inland.

idp.text: Saudi Arabia is a party to the 1968 Vienna Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1949 Geneva one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1968 Vienna version. A permit issued under the 1949 Geneva Convention carries no treaty obligation here.

source.name: UN Treaty Collection — Convention on Road Traffic (Vienna, 1968), status of parties
source.instrument: Convention on Road Traffic, Vienna, 8 November 1968 (UNTS vol. 1042, p. 17)

driving.text: Saudi Arabia is a party to the 1968 Vienna Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1949 Geneva one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1968 Vienna version. A permit issued under the 1949 Geneva Convention carries no treaty obligation here. Whether a permit is required in addition to a national license, and for how long a foreign license may be used, are set by national road law and have not been checked for Saudi Arabia yet.

source.name: UN Treaty Collection — Convention on Road Traffic (Vienna, 1968), status of parties
source.instrument: Convention on Road Traffic, Vienna, 8 November 1968 (UNTS vol. 1042, p. 17)

tips.text: Alcohol is completely banned in Saudi Arabia — there are no licensed bars for tourists, and importing or possessing any amount is a criminal offense.
Dress rules for tourists have relaxed — abayas are not required for foreign women — but both men and women should dress modestly in public, covering shoulders and knees.
During Ramadan, avoid eating, drinking or smoking in public during daylight hours; opening hours shift and many restaurants close until sunset.
Women aged 18+ can now visit Saudi Arabia independently — no male guardian or male travel companion is required for tourist entry.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Saudi Arabia?
faq.answer: Yes. US passport holders need a tourist eVisa (applied for at visa.visitsaudi.com) or a visa on arrival at major airports. Both cost roughly SAR 300 including mandatory medical insurance and give a one-year, multiple-entry visa with stays of up to 90 days.

faq.question: How much does the Saudi tourist eVisa cost?
faq.answer: Roughly SAR 300 (about USD 80) in total, which includes the compulsory medical insurance automatically bundled with every eVisa. The exact amount is shown at checkout — apply only on the official portal visa.visitsaudi.com.

faq.question: Can I get a Saudi visa on arrival with a US, UK or Schengen visa?
faq.answer: Yes. Holders of a valid US, UK or Schengen visa that has already been used at least once (or a UK/US/EU residence permit) can obtain a visa on arrival regardless of whether their nationality is on the eVisa list — a route often used by Indian, Pakistani and Filipino travelers. Confirm current conditions on visa.visitsaudi.com before flying.

faq.question: Can I perform Umrah on a tourist eVisa, and what vaccinations do pilgrims need?
faq.answer: Yes — tourist eVisa holders may perform Umrah (outside the Hajj season). Hajj requires a separate Hajj visa issued through official quota channels. All pilgrims must carry a valid quadrivalent meningococcal ACWY vaccination certificate, issued at least 10 days before arrival, and seasonal extra requirements can apply depending on your departure country.

faq.question: Is alcohol allowed in Saudi Arabia?
faq.answer: No. Alcohol is prohibited throughout the country for tourists — it cannot be imported, purchased or consumed, and violations are criminal offenses. Duty-free alcohol bought en route must not be carried into the country.
